blocks.text: In this game, you play by the same rules without Tabletop Simulator.
The base game plays through the “Heart of Sinnoh Campaign” with the following objectives split over three acts:

items.text: Liberate your home village.
Obtain the three Shards.
Restore the Heart of Sinnoh and reach the Temple of Sinnoh for the final confrontation.

blocks.text: The first trainer to conquer all the objectives may claim victory.

items.text: Ensure all trainers have selected a seat.
The first trainer to choose a home village card is the last person to have seen a friend or relative from where they call home. This continues anti-clockwise until all trainers have selected a card:
Choose one of the two starter Pokémon and add it to your party.
Find the corresponding trainer token and place it on your village.
Place your home village card in your hand and it will automatically change your hand colour to the correct one.
Important: Now change your player colour to the new colour of the seat where your home village card is.
Select the “Heart of Sinnoh Campaign” and click “Start Game”.
Draw the “Prologue” card from the acts deck and follow its instructions.
The trainer who was last to choose their home village card takes the first turn of the game. Turns then continue clockwise.

blocks.text: In this game, you choose the campaign, home village and starter Pokémon when setting up the game, and the game places the tokens, colours and cards for you.

You may move up to 3 tiles per turn at the start of the game. The only restriction to movement is that you cannot move onto tiles that are 2 or more full elevations higher or lower than your current tile.
You may interact with things on the map whilst standing on their tile:

items.text: When you are on the same tile as another trainer, you can freely trade with them or challenge them to a battle (if they are outside of a village, the challenge cannot be denied).
You may continue to interact with things on the map until all of your movement for the turn runs out, but your turn immediately ends after any battle.

blocks.text: You may take each of these actions once per turn whilst at any village:

items.text: Fully restore your entire party: Remove all damage and status effects from your Pokémon.
Exchange your Apricorns with the Ginkgo Merchants according to one or both of the current Ginkgo Trades being offered (top-right of the map). Shuffle the Ginkgo Trade deck afterwards.
Fly to another village by discarding 1 Apricorn (there must be no Team Galactic Grunts on either village).

blocks.text: In this game, you see and choose the current Ginkgo Trades on screen, and the game shuffles the deck for you.

Higher encounter tiers are tougher to defeat and capture but grant more Journey Points.
Encounter tier icons (Weak · Moderate · Strong · Legendary)
To search for a Pokémon, have your trainer token stand on an Apricorn Tree or Apricorn Reef and press the “Search” button on the Pokédex.

The Pokédex will return Weak 3 / Moderate 2 / Strong 1 Pokémon. Once you decide to search, you must choose one of the Pokémon to battle but you may still craft items like Poké Balls before the battle begins.
Legendary Pokémon can be encountered in two ways:

items.text: Artifact Legendary Pokémon: Can only be encountered at their home location if you are holding the matching Artifact [[hidden_spots.artifacts|see Artifacts]].
Shrine Legendary Pokémon: Can only be encountered at their home shrine after their event card is drawn from the Shrine Events deck [[shrines.legendary|see Legendary Events]].

blocks.text: In this game, the game draws the cards from the encounter deck for you when you search.
Apricorns are your primary crafting resource [[crafting.intro|see Crafting]] and are obtained by defeating or capturing the wild Pokémon that guards them.
Apricorns Trees provide up to 3 Apricorns of one type whereas Apricorn Reefs provide up to 3 Apricorns of usually a variety of types [[battle.rewards|see Rewards]].
Apricorn Tree
Apricorn Reef
Tier 1 · Tier 2 · Tier 3
During a battle with a wild Pokémon, you may use one of your Poké Balls instead of attacking on your turn.
The quality of the Poké Ball determines how many dice to roll. For example, the standard Poké Ball lets you roll 3 Typeless attack dice during a capture roll.
Poké Ball [[crafting.balls|see Crafting]]
To successfully capture the Pokémon, the result of your roll needs to be equal to or greater than the Capture Rate of the wild Pokémon.
Capture Accuracy: If the Pokémon you are trying to capture has been inflicted with any status effects, replace 1 status symbol with 1 regular hit.

If successful, place the Pokémon along with any damage, status effects and items on it into an empty Pokémon slot in your trainer area. If you do not have an empty slot, you may release an existing Pokémon in your party to make room (discard the released Pokémon along with any moves it knows).
Additionally, place the Poké Ball used to capture it in the Poké Ball slot beneath the Pokémon (cannot be used again to capture more Pokémon):

items.text: This can be used to transport your Pokémon (and anything on it) to the top or bottom side of the arena [[automation.moving|see Automation]].
Also can be flipped over to indicate your Pokémon has fainted.

blocks.text: If unsuccessful, discard the Poké Ball and the battle continues (you may get a chance to throw another Poké Ball on your next turn).
In this game, the game handles the Poké Ball slot, moving to the arena and marking fainted Pokémon for you.
During your turn and whilst outside of battle, you may evolve your Pokémon by discarding Journey Points equal to the Evolve Cost of the Pokémon.

Fully restore the Pokémon, place it in the slot above the “Evolve” button on the Pokédex and then press the button. Take the evolution card from the Pokédex and place it in your trainer area (if there is a choice, like with Eevee, choose one and return the rest to the deck). Items and taught moves are carried over to the evolved Pokémon.

You may teach the move of the old Pokémon to the newly evolved Pokémon (regardless of the types it can learn) by flipping the old card over and placing it under the new card. Otherwise discard the old card.
Budew with just the move Grass Whistle.
Secondary evolution has its own move plus the move from Budew.
In this game, the game takes out the evolution card and moves the old card for you.
Legendary Pokémon act differently to regular Pokémon in two ways:

items.text: Legendary Pokémon flee the battle after defeating all your Pokémon instead of defeating just one.
Legendary Pokémon get access to their own special tactics by default.

blocks.text: To access the special tactics, place the Legendary Pokémon in the arena. When captured, you can add/remove moves to overwrite/reveal these tactics (Alpha Strike is always overwritten before Beast Boost).

items.text: Alpha Strike (Attack): Provides an attack that can be any learnable type of the Legendary Pokémon. However, its attack strength is decreased to 2 if this move was used last turn.
Beast Boost (Ability): Triggers whenever the Pokémon battling the Legendary Pokémon faints. Its battle fatigue is decreased by 3 whilst increasing the attack strength of the next attack it uses by 1.

blocks.text: Special tactics that Legendary Pokémon can use in battle.
Alpha Pokémon, Ultra Beasts and the Ultra Burst are special types of Legendary Pokémon (the last two are exclusive to the Ultra Burst campaign).
Alpha Pokémon
Ultra Beasts
The Ultra Burst
Certain Pokémon have multiple forms that are accessible by changing the state of their cards.
Cherrim — Cherrim after using the move Gather Sunlight: Sunshine Form
Shaymin — Shaymin whilst holding the Gracidea Flower: Sky Form
Form changes during battle by using a move

items.text: Neither battle fatigue or the current turn order is affected when changing form.
When the battle ends, the Pokémon returns to its default form (State 1).
If a form changing move has been taught to a Pokémon without the form it specifies, ignore the form change.

blocks.text: Form changes outside of battle by holding an item

items.text: You may change to the form specified by the item whilst outside of battle.
If the Pokémon is no longer holding the item, it returns to its default form (State 1).

blocks.text: If you defeat a wild Pokémon with different signature moves on its forms, you can teach any of the signature moves to your Pokémon.
In this game, the game changes the form for you instead of changing card states.
Before continuing with the rules, this section will hopefully inform you of all the automation features available in Legends of Sinnoh.
In this game, the game handles all of the Tabletop Simulator automation features below for you.
Apricorns and Journey Points can be moved to and from your bag using the buttons provided in your trainer area. Left click will put the item into your bag, right click will discard the item.
Bag buttons
In this game, the game keeps count of your Apricorns and Journey Points.
The thematic way to get around, you can click the centre of a village to have a Staraptor transport your trainer token to that village [[overview.village|see Villages for rules]].
Fly to Sunyshore Village
In this game, the game moves your trainer token when you choose to fly.
Each of the Dice Roller panels in the arena calculate the bonus/penalty damage from type effectiveness automatically when selecting a move type.
By having the small green button toggled on, you can search through all move types instead of just the ones your currently active Pokémon can learn.
Dice Roller
In this game, the game calculates type effectiveness damage.

Pokémon in this game can end up with many objects on them as they learn new moves, hold items and take damage/status effects. To move all of these objects together easily, you can instead use the Poké Ball token of the Pokémon to move them about.
Poké Ball token in your trainer area linked to Infernape.
Poké Ball token moved to the arena, Infernape along with any moves, items and dice are moved to the arena also.
Important: Make sure to increase your lift height in Tabletop Simulator if you are having trouble with the Poké Balls linking to other Pokémon in your party accidently when moving them around.
In this game, the game moves the Pokémon together with its moves, held items and dice.
The trainer who initiated the battle sends out their first Pokémon before the other trainer but gets to claim the Initiative Advantage token in exchange.
The Initiative Advantage token
Both Pokémon compare their initiative values. The Pokémon with the higher initiative takes the first turn. Turns then continue back and forth between the two until a Pokémon faints.

If there is a tie for initiative, the trainer with the Initiative Advantage token may use it to win the tie but the token is then passed to the other trainer. If the token is not used, the other trainer automatically wins the tie.
Choose one of your moves. Roll attack dice equal to the attack strength of the move and then resolve any effects of the move. Deal damage equal to the dice result plus any effects/bonuses.
Type effectiveness is considered as positive/negative bonus damage and fully stacks when attacking a Pokémon with two types:

items.text: Super Effective: +2 damage
Not Very Effective: -2 damage
Not Effective: -4 damage

blocks.text: The “Typeless” type, ignores type effectiveness

items.text: When the opposing Pokémon faints: You may switch out before your opponent sends in their next Pokémon. Turn order is reset, initiative values are then compared to see which Pokémon goes first.
When you use a move effect that allows you to switch out: Turn order is maintained, your opponent always takes their turn next.

blocks.text: Any battle can be ended early by conceding after one of your Pokémon faints. All damage and status effects remain after battle.

items.text: A trainer is out of usable Pokémon or concedes: Their opponent is declared as the winner of the battle if they still have usable Pokémon, otherwise it is considered a draw.
The wild Pokémon has been captured or faints: Captured Pokémon are added to your party, fainted Pokémon are discarded. You still get the full rewards even if your Pokémon faints at the same time.
The wild Pokémon flees the battle: Wild Pokémon that have not fainted during battle are returned to their deck.
Weak, Moderate and Strong wild Pokémon flee the battle after defeating one of your Pokémon.
Legendary wild Pokémon flee the battle after defeating all your Pokémon.

blocks.text: After winning a battle against another trainer:

items.text: You may take 1 Artifact of your choice from them or take up to 2 of their Change of Fate cards from them at random.
You and the other trainer may not be challenged again until the start of your next turns.

blocks.text: After a wild Pokémon flees:

items.text: You gain Weak 2 / Moderate 1 / Strong 0 of the 3 Apricorns it was guarding.

blocks.text: After a wild Pokémon is captured or faints:

items.text: You gain Weak 1 / Moderate 2 / Strong 3 / Legendary 4 Journey Points.
You gain all 3 Apricorns it was guarding.

blocks.text: Additionally, only after a wild Pokémon faints:

items.text: You gain an extra 2 Journey Points.
You may teach its move to a Pokémon in your party where the Move Type matches one of the Learnable Move Types:
Moves that are Typeless can be taught to any Pokémon.
Pokémon can only have 3 moves in total, but the signature move cannot be changed. Existing moves can be replaced by discarding them.

blocks.text: If you are out of usable Pokémon:

items.text: You are immediately returned to your home village and your party is automatically fully restored at the start of your next turn.
Draw 1 Change of Fate card when you start your next turn.
All status effects are persistent until a Pokémon can heal them (through fully restoring, fainting or effects that heal statuses).
A Pokémon that already has a status effect cannot be afflicted with any further status effects (however two status effects can be inflicted through special moves that inflict them simultaneously).

head: Status
Effect
Immunity
rows: When attacking, take 3 damage if you use the same move as you used last turn.
When attacking, reduce the total damage you deal by 2.
Reduce your initiative by 3. Only on your immediate next attack, remove all regular hits from the roll.
At the end of your turns during battle, take 2 damage. Ignore when the battle ends. You may no longer heal damage.
When attacked, increase the attack strength of moves against you by 2. You may no longer switch out or flee the battle.
When attacking, replace 1 regular hit with 1 status symbol. When attacked, replace 1 regular hit with 1 critical hit.

items.text: During battle, a Pokémon becomes fatigued after 5 dice rolls in a row.
Whilst fatigued, deal 3 damage to it every time its dice roller is used.
When a Pokémon switches out, it resets its battle fatigue back to 0.

blocks.text: In this game, the game counts the rolls instead of the dice roller.

In this example, we will be battling the wild Pokémon Leafeon with our Flareon. First, we compare initiative and see that both Flareon and Leafeon have 10 initiative each. Since we initiated the battle, we start with the Initiative Advantage token and use it to go first.
Their Dice Roller · Damage Dice · Wild Leafeon · Attack Dice · Your Flareon · Status Dice · Your Dice Roller
Turn 1
We choose to use Fire Blast against Leafeon:

items.text: On the dice roller, we set the number of dice to roll to 5 as this is the attack strength of this move.
Also, on the dice roller, we set the type of the move to Fire as this is the type of this move. We get a +2 damage bonus from being super effective against the Grass-type of Leafeon.

blocks.text: Dice Roller set to 5 Dice and the Fire type.
After clicking Roll, we get a below average result:

items.text: 2 status symbols (0 damage each)
2 regular hits (1 damage each)
1 critical hit (2 damage each)

blocks.text: The dice result adds up to 4 damage. By including our super effective bonus (+2), we will do a total of 6 damage to Leafeon (place a Damage Dice with value set to 6 on Leafeon).
Dice roll result adds up to 4 damage.

However, lets also read the effect of Fire Blast: “If 2 or more status symbols are rolled: Inflict the Burned status on the target.” Since we rolled 2 status symbols, Leafeon is now Burned as a result (place a Status Dice with value set to Burned on Leafeon also).
Damage Dice set to 6 and Status Dice set to Burned.
Turn 2
Now Leafeon gets to attack and can only use Leaf Blade:

items.text: Because Grass is not very effective against the Fire-type of Flareon, total damage will be reduced by 2.

blocks.text: After hitting roll, they get an above average result:

items.text: 3 regular hits (1 damage each)
1 critical hit (2 damage each)

blocks.text: Dice Roller set to 4 Dice and the Grass type.

The dice result adds up to 5 damage. But by including type effectiveness (-2), the reduced damage from Leafeon being Burned (-2) and the effect of Leaf Blade on critical hits (+1) this means Flareon only takes 2 damage (place a Damage Dice with value set to 2 on Flareon).
Dice roll result adds up to 5 damage.
Damage Dice set to 2.
Finishing the Battle
Flareon finishes the battle with another Fire Blast (no matter the dice result, the super effective damage is enough to remove the remaining 2 health of Leafeon).
The trainer may now claim the rewards for defeating Leafeon as well as teach Leaf Blade to a Pokémon in their party if they wish to.
Flareon card for reference.
Leafeon card for reference.
In this game, the game sets the dice roller and places the dice for you.
You may trigger a Swarm Battle by clicking “Search” on the Pokédex whilst you are at a Distortion Gate.
There are 4 Distortion Gates found across the region:

items.text: Snowdrift Gate (Plains Biome Pokémon)
Lilly Gate (Mountain Biome Pokémon)
Westbreeze Gate (Ocean Biome Pokémon)
Deepmarsh Gate (Forest Biome Pokémon)

blocks.text: The Distortion Gates
Swarm Battles follow these rules:

items.text: They may be triggered in both campaigns at active and inactive Distortion Gates. Swarm Battles count as wild encounters.
The battle consists of a Weak Pokémon, a Moderate Pokémon and a Strong Pokémon. The Pokémon enter the battle in this same order (manually move their cards instead of using the “Battle!” buttons).
The wild Pokémon form their own party and only flee after defeating all your Pokémon.
If every Pokémon in the wild Pokémon party has been defeated or captured, you gain 7 Journey Points as the total reward for this battle. You do not gain any Journey Points if you lose.

blocks.text: Example of a Swarm Battle at the Deepmarsh Gate.
In this game, the game brings the three Pokémon into the battle for you.

blocks.q: What is considered as the damage from an attack?
blocks.text: Attacks deal their damage to the opposing Pokémon by adding together:

items.text: The result of the dice roll after all dice modifications are resolved.
The type effectiveness bonus/penalty damage.
Any extra damage from the effect of the move itself.

blocks.q: How do attacks that deal double damage work?
blocks.text: Take the damage from the attack (see above) and multiply it by 2. Status effects like being Burned or the armour effect from Prism Armour only affect the total damage being dealt, so are applied after the attack damage is first doubled.

blocks.q: In what order is damage/healing applied?
blocks.text: During a turn, all damage and healing effects are applied simultaneously. Any effects that state they occur at the end of a turn are considered separately to those during the turn and are also applied simultaneously.

blocks.q: Does the damage bonus from type effectiveness still apply even if my dice result deals no damage?
blocks.text: Yes, the type effectiveness bonus is always applied with the attack even if you would otherwise deal no damage. The same applies to any extra damage from the effect of the move.

blocks.q: In a battle between two trainers, who sends out their next Pokémon first if both Pokémon faint simultaneously?
blocks.text: The trainer who currently has Initiative Advantage does so.

blocks.q: Is initiative just speed from the console games?
blocks.text: Not quite, Pokémon in this game take it in turns to use attacks rather than doing so simultaneously. Initiative determines which of the two Pokémon gets to have their turn first. When initiative is rechecked, the turn order is completely reset.

blocks.q: Do effects that add dice to another attack count for the effect of that attack?
blocks.text: Yes, for example, I can use Bubble Beam which adds 2 status symbols to the next attack against the target and then use a move like Blizzard which inflicts the Frozen status on the target if 2 status symbols are rolled to guarantee the effect triggers.

blocks.q: Can a move be reduced to 0 attack strength?
blocks.text: No, all moves have a minimum of 1 attack strength.

blocks.q: If a move has a maximum attack strength in its effect, can its attack strength be increased by other effects?
blocks.text: Yes, the maximum attack strength only applies to the effect of the move itself. However, all moves have a maximum of 9 total attack strength.

blocks.q: Can the effect of a move stack with itself?
blocks.text: No, this is most notable for effects that apply until the user switches out.

If you were unable to find the answer to your question here, I encourage you to use your best judgement before asking in the #help channel of the Discord server. The channel is not a replacement for reading the rules.

Required for catching Pokémon [[pokemon.capture|see Capturing Pokémon]].

blocks.text: Journey Stamps are collected as you experience certain aspects of the game and grant you rewards for doing so. Once a stamp is received, it is kept for the remainder of the game.
Found at the bottom-right of your trainer area, the stamp sheet can be filled using the Decal tool in Tabletop Simulator.
Stamp sheet
In this game, the game stamps the sheet for you when a condition is met.
Stamps can be claimed in any order and are immediately awarded upon their condition being met. The conditions for each stamp are as follows:
Top row, left to right:

items.text: You fail to capture a wild Pokémon 2 turns in a row during a battle.
You win a battle against another trainer or an Ultra Beast.
You have at least 1 of every Apricorn type in your bag.
You have captured a Legendary Pokémon.

blocks.text: Bottom row, left to right:

items.text: You have 3 or more held items equipped in your party.
You have been victorious at a Swarm Battle.
You have 3 different Change of Fate cards in your hand.

blocks.text: Use the button at the bottom-right of the stamp sheet to flip over to the rewards side to see what you get when you reach each milestone.
Stamp rewards may be claimed immediately after reaching each milestone:

items.text: Gain 1 Red, 1 Blue and 1 Yellow Apricorn.
Randomly draw 5 Weak Pokémon cards, store them next to your trainer area. You may teach these cards as moves to your Pokémon.
Gain 1 Pink, 1 Green and 1 White Apricorn.
Randomly draw 5 Moderate Pokémon cards, store them next to your trainer area. You may teach these cards as moves to your Pokémon.
Gain 3 Black Apricorns.
Randomly draw 5 Strong Pokémon cards, store them next to your trainer area. You may teach these cards as moves to your Pokémon.
Gain a Scroll of Nobility that allows you to use the Noble Form (State 2) of any fully evolved Starter Pokémon when held.

blocks.text: In this game, the game flips the sheet and gives you the rewards.

Scattered across the Sinnoh region you will find both Regular Hidden Spots and Special Hidden Spots that you may interact with when you pass over them. Flip the Hidden Spot token over to reveal what it is and resolve its effect.
Regular Hidden Spot · Special Hidden Spot

Gain 1, 2 or 3 Apricorns of the type and quantity shown on the token. These stashes are a great way to progress quickly, especially if you find the elusive Black Apricorns. Discard Apricorn Stash token afterwards.
Red Apricorn Stash [3 of each type]

Campsites allow you to fully restore your party and trade with the Ginkgo Merchants once per turn like villages do [[overview.village|see Villages]], however you cannot fly to or from them. Campsite tokens remain on the map after being found.
Campsite [6 in total]
Draw 2 Change of Fate cards when revealed. Place the token on an empty Fallen Star spot afterwards (where the Change of Fate cards are).
For every 4 Fallen Stars collected: All trainers draw 1 Change of Fate card at the start of their turns for the rest of the game.
Fallen Star [8 in total]
When revealed, you are forced to battle an Alpha Pokémon. Since the Alpha Pokémon is the initiator, they start with Initiative Advantage.
Stand on the token and use the Pokédex to “Search” for the Pokémon to attach this token to as a held item.
Alpha Pokémon [6 in total]

The token increases the health of the user by 4 and reclassifies the user as a Legendary Pokémon. This means it gains access to the move Alpha Strike and the ability Beast Boost as well as requiring a 6+ roll to capture and rewarding 4 Journey Points by default.

You keep the token if you capture the Alpha Pokémon, but the token cannot be unequipped. The token is discarded when the Pokémon holding it is discarded or returned to the deck. This means it does not remain on the map if you lose the battle.
The health of Floatzel is increased to 11 when equipped with the Alpha Pokémon token.
In this game, when the token is revealed the game finds the Pokémon and attaches the token to it.

Once per turn, you may discard an Apricorn whilst at any Shrine to draw 1 Shrine Event card. Resolve the effect of the card once drawn.

Offering an Apricorn from a higher tier will usually increase the strength of the event (look for text separated by “/” on the card). If the deck is out of cards, shuffle the discard pile back into the deck.
By additionally discarding 7 Journey Points, you may draw 3 cards in total and choose 2 of them (immediately discard the card not chosen).
When there are 4 or more trainers, Shrine Blessing effects are also given to another trainer. You always get to apply the effect of the event first.
All trainers gain the Apricorns specified on the card.
Find the corresponding Legendary Pokémon token and place it on the Shrine specified on the card.
The token is removed from the game once the Legendary Pokémon is defeated or captured. You cannot make a Shrine Offering at their Shrine whilst the token is there.
A Song of Frost heralds the arrival of Articuno.
In this game, the game places the Legendary Pokémon token for you.
A special type of Legendary Event where all trainers gain 1 Change of Fate card instead of any Apricorns.
Each trainer may change their Follower token in secret (flip your token face-down and then change the state).

After revealing all Follower changes, place the God of Sinnoh token (Dialga, Palkia or Giratina) with the most Followers on the Origin Shrine (you choose if tied, replaces any God of Sinnoh token already there).
Celestial Fractures upset the balance of power across Sinnoh.
In this game, the game handles choosing Followers and placing the God of Sinnoh token for you.
The Gods of Sinnoh radiate with powers far greater than those of the lesser Legendary Pokémon:

items.text: When encountered at the Origin Shrine, if you do not posses their matching Celestial Artifact: They require a roll of 7 to capture and after their first form is defeated, they proceed to their second form (State 2) fully restored.
Whilst a God of Sinnoh token is at the Origin Shrine: All of their Followers gain 1 extra movement per turn.

blocks.text: A God of Sinnoh token is removed from the game once it is defeated or captured. You cannot make a Shrine Offering at the Origin Shrine whilst it is there (this is relevant for Act III of the Heart of Sinnoh campaign).
Each trainer starts with a face down Follower token (on their bag). Once face up, the token has 3 states indicating which God of Sinnoh you are a Follower of.
Flip your Follower token face up as soon as you become a Follower of any God of Sinnoh (this will be when the first Celestial Fracture event is drawn).
Giratina · Dialga · Palkia
When any two trainers are Followers of the same God of Sinnoh:

items.text: They may trade remotely.

blocks.text: When any two trainers are Followers of different Gods of Sinnoh:

items.text: They may battle remotely (these remote battle requests can be denied).

blocks.text: In this game, the game flips the Follower token for you.
You may keep up to 5 Change of Fate cards in your hand. During your battles and during your turn outside of battle, you may play 1 effect per turn.

Each card has a Play 3 effect which can be used if 3 of the same card are played together. Your Follower token is always counted as 1 of the cards needed for the Play 3 effect matching your God of Sinnoh.
Discard all played cards. If the Change of Fate deck is out of cards, shuffle the discard pile back into the deck.
A Follower of Dialga only needs to play 2 Dialga cards to use the “Reroll Any” effect

items.text: Dialga: Individually reroll 1 dice. The Play 3 effect allows you to individually reroll any of the dice rolled, once each.
Palkia: Instantly move to any tile up to 3 tiles away, regardless of elevation. The Play 3 effect allows you to instantly move to any tile on the map.
Giratina:
Before attacking, deal 2 damage to your active Pokémon to increase the attack strength of their next move by 1.
The Play 3 effect deals damage equal to your active Pokémon’s current health to increase the attack strength of their next move by half the damage taken, rounded down.
Your active Pokémon gets to use their next move even if they faint to either Sacrifice effect. Maximum attack strength of all moves is 9.
Arceus: Counts as any 1 card towards all other Play 3 effects. This Play 3 effect grants you 1 Blessing of Arceus during the Ultra Burst campaign.
Equivalent Exchange: You may search the deck or discard pile. All moves are kept even if the new Pokémon cannot normally learn these moves. Notably, any Alpha Pokémon tokens are kept.
Splendid Banquet: When giving this effect to another trainer, they can choose the Apricorn Stews they want when it is their turn (place the event card in front of them so they remember).

blocks.text: In this game, instead of placing the card in front of them, the game remembers and lets that trainer choose on their turn.
In the future, a pivotal battle for the fate of the world has been lost.

By harnessing the powers of the legendary Pokémon Dialga and Palkia, Team Galactic have travelled to our own time to shatter the Heart of Sinnoh, a primordial jewel that embodies the spirit of the world.
To prevent retribution whilst their plans are finalised, grunts have been dispatched to subdue the villages of the region.
Place one “Team Galactic Grunts” token on the home villages of each trainer face-up.
To progress with your journey and ultimately win the game, you will need to defeat Team Galactic in a series of battles determined by the act cards (found on the Heart of Sinnoh campaign base).
In this game, the game places the Grunts tokens and act cards for you.
Team Galactic get access to special tactics in battle by placing their Pokémon in the arena:

items.text: Plan B (Attack): A Typeless attack that allows the Team Galactic trainer to strike at more opportune time by adding 1 damage to their Galactic Retribution ability.

Galactic Retribution (Ability): During a battle, allows Team Galactic to strike back by storing damage dice on this ability whenever their Pokémon faint. When one of their Pokémon is attacked, you may move all the stored damage dice to the target.

blocks.text: Special tactics that Team Galactic can use in battle.
In battles with Team Galactic:

items.text: Have another trainer control the Pokémon of Team Galactic (if playing solo, this is left up to you to decide).
As the initiator, you start with Initiative Advantage.
Each time a Team Galactic Pokémon faints, the trainer controlling them may then choose which Pokémon to send in next from the remaining non-fainted Pokémon they have available.
Team Galactic Pokémon are unable to switch out after defeating one of your Pokémon (this can be overruled if you want more challenging battles).

blocks.text: At the start of Act I, you gain 3 Red Apricorns.
Your first objective is to defeat the Team Galactic Grunts at your home village. Other trainers cannot liberate your village for you.
You cannot fly to or from your home village whilst the Grunts occupy it, but you can still heal your Pokémon and exchange Apricorns there.
Grunt Battle
When ready, return to your home village to start the battle:

items.text: Shuffle the Team Galactic Grunts deck and randomly draw 2 of them face-up.
If you defeat both Pokémon (whilst still being able to battle), you are victorious:
Gain +2 movement per turn for the rest of the game.
Remove the Team Galactic Grunts token from your village.

blocks.text: If you are the first trainer to have liberated their home village, draw the Act II card. Other trainers still must finish Act I.
During Act II, you will need to collect the three Shards. To achieve this, battle the Team Galactic Commander stationed at each lake around the Sinnoh region. You can collect the Shards in any order:

head: Shard
Commander
rows: Battle Commander Mars at Lake Verity.
Battle Commander Jupiter at Lake Acuity.
Battle Commander Saturn at Lake Valor.

blocks.text: Shard of Emotion · Shard of Knowledge · Shard of Willpower
Lake Commander Battles
When ready, travel to one of the lakes to start the battle:

items.text: The trainer controlling the Commander chooses 2/3/4 (increases for each Shard you already have) of the 5 Pokémon for that Commander (from the Team Galactic Commanders deck) and displays them face-up.
If you defeat all their Pokémon (whilst still being able to battle), you are victorious:
Gain the corresponding Shard.
Each Shard increases your maximum party size by 1.

blocks.text: If you are the first trainer to have collected all three Shards, draw the Act III card. Other trainers still must finish Act II.

The final test for you and your team. Head to the Origin Shrine (at the top of the central mountain) and make a Shrine Offering there to restore the Heart of Sinnoh from your three Shards (the Shards are not discarded).
If there is a God of Sinnoh token on the Origin Shrine, you cannot make your Shrine Offering until they are defeated or captured.
To prevent any stalemates with other trainers, if you are victorious against a God of Sinnoh in this campaign, you may immediately take another turn.
The Heart of Sinnoh
When the Heart is restored, you gain the Heart of Sinnoh held item which is required to battle Cyrus.
Whilst held, it increases the attack strength of moves that are the same type as the user by 1.
The Heart of Sinnoh [1 per trainer]
Cyrus Battle
Proceed to the Temple of Sinnoh to start the battle with Cyrus:

items.text: The trainer controlling Cyrus chooses 6 of his 8 Pokémon (from the Team Galactic Boss deck) and displays them face-up.
If you defeat all 6 Pokémon (whilst still being able to battle), you are victorious:
Draw the Ending card.

blocks.text: The trainer that defeats Cyrus gets to choose whether to be the Hero of Sinnoh or the Traitor of Sinnoh.
If you choose the Hero of Sinnoh option, you are immediately crowned as the winner of the game.
If you choose the Traitor of Sinnoh option:

items.text: Turns stop and all trainers have their parties fully restored.
You must now challenge each of your fellow trainers to battle in any order you choose (as the initiator, you start with Initiative Advantage).
Each time you defeat a trainer, fully restore your party and return any Change of Fate cards used to your hand.
If any of the trainers defeat you, the game ends with them as the winner of the game instead.
If you defeat all the other trainers, you win the game and are crowned as the undisputed strongest trainer!

blocks.text: Note from the Game Designer
If time allows, it is recommended that trainers always choose the Traitor of Sinnoh option after their first playthrough of the game.

Once you know what Pokémon Cyrus has, it becomes easier to counter him from the start. However, your fellow trainers are not so predictable. This leads to a more rewarding team building and endgame experience, whilst giving everyone a chance at victory!
10 years have passed since the events that saw the Heart of Sinnoh restored and Team Galactic forced to retreat.

With the light of the Heart emanating across the region, a time of prosperity has descended upon Sinnoh. This has attracted new trainers from regions afar but also the attention of mysterious entities from beyond the bounds of this dimension…

Without warning, a beast of pure light bursts through into the Distortion World, the counterbalance to our world, threatening to cast Sinnoh into total darkness. As the breach becomes increasingly unstable, more beasts spew forth wrecking havoc across the land.
Trainers from across the region must now work together to draw power away from the Ultra Burst and defeat the beast at its core before the light of our world is consumed forever.
The Ultra Burst Campaign adds a new area to the map, the Distortion World, with Necrozma residing at its centre.

The Ultra Beasts, represented by 9 figurines, are scattered across Sinnoh at the start of the game. Each time all trainers have taken a turn, click the button tracking “Breach Strength” next to the Distortion World to allow the Ultra Beasts to take their movement turn.

Your only objective is to defeat Necrozma before the breach reaches its critical threshold (70%), otherwise you lose. It is recommended that you defeat the majority of the Ultra Beasts first to weaken Necrozma!
In this game, the game runs the Ultra Beasts' turn once every trainer has taken a turn.

Unlike the Heart of Sinnoh campaign, you start with 3 Red, 3 Blue and 3 Yellow Apricorns and all 6 Pokémon slots unlocked. Furthermore, this campaign has several difficulty levels that determine how many Blessings of Arceus you as a group start with:

items.text: New Trainer: 3 Blessings of Arceus
Veteran Trainer: 1 Blessing of Arceus
Master Trainer: 0 Blessings of Arceus

blocks.text: New Trainer · Veteran Trainer · Master Trainer
Blessing of Arceus: Use to skip a movement turn of the Ultra Beasts or revive an eliminated trainer.
Blessing of Arceus
Repeat the same setup steps as in the base game but toggle the selected campaign to the “Ultra Burst Campaign” before pressing “Start Game”.
In this game, you choose the campaign when setting up the game, and the game hands out the starting Apricorns and party slots for you.
Necrozma and the Ultra Beasts protect themselves using Prism Armour. For every 2 Prism Armour tokens: Reduce the total damage taken per turn by 1.

items.text: Self-inflicted damage, fatigue damage and status effect damage (notably Poison) are examples of damage that may be reduced during their turns.
Attack damage is the primary example of damage that may be reduced during your turns.

blocks.text: Prism Armour tokens are found on the campaign board.
At the start of the game, place all 9 Prism Armour tokens on the Ultra Burst side and no tokens on the Ultra Beast side of the Prism Armour areas.
So to begin with, Necrozma takes 4 less damage per turn whereas the Ultra Beasts take no less damage per turn.
When an Ultra Beast is defeated, move a Prism Armour token from the Ultra Burst side to the Ultra Beast side.
Ultra Burst side now starts with 9 Prism Armour but now has 8 after an Ultra Beast is defeated. Ultra Beast side starts with 0 Prism Armour but now has 1 after an Ultra Beast is defeated.
In this game, the game moves the Prism Armour tokens and reduces the damage for you.
As the breach grows stronger, Pokémon start to experience strange effects that have seeped out from the Distortion World.
At every increment of 10% breach strength, trainers will be dealt a random Distortion Breach card that they must attach to a Pokémon in their party.

These cards are attached to the Pokémon like a move but grant a passive ability instead (like Galactic Retribution and Beast Boost). If it is not possible to attach the card when it is dealt, keep the card in your hand and attach it as soon as possible.
Distortion Breach card with the Reckless Assault ability.
Any action that leads to a Distortion Breach card leaving your party is not allowed. However, when an Ultra Beast is defeated, all trainers may discard or move 1 Distortion Breach card.
Reckless Assault ability added to a Roselia.
The Ultra Beasts start with 4 tile moves per turn shared between all of them. Additionally, Necrozma will remotely target a number of tiles at random based on the number of players in the game:
Tiles targeted by Necrozma for each number of players
At every increment of 10% breach strength, the number of tile moves the Ultra Beasts have in total increases by 1.
What we have observed so far about how the Ultra Beasts interact with the world around them:

items.text: Hidden Spots: These are sent into the Distortion World (or are discarded if there are no more free tiles).
Apricorn Trees/Reefs and Shrines: These are destroyed preventing all further interactions with those tokens by trainers (the tokens themselves become darker in colour when this happens).
Villages and Legendary Locations: They seem to steer clear of these places for unknown reasons.
The breach grows in strength when Apricorn Trees/Reefs or Shrines are destroyed by the Ultra Beasts or Necrozma.

blocks.text: To initiate a battle with an Ultra Beast or Necrozma, click “Search” whilst standing on one of their tokens. They are treated like any other Legendary Pokémon for tactics and rewards but cannot be captured.
To decide which moves they use in battle, you can have another player control them or you can follow these principles in order:

items.text: Prioritise trying to use their signature move if it makes sense to.
Use the move that gives the highest value when you add together: Attack strength + Type effectiveness bonus + Move effect damage

blocks.text: If a trainer is defeated by Necrozma, they are eliminated from the game.
The Ultra Beasts and Necrozma are fully restored between battle attempts and phases.
Necrozma has 3 phases that can be selected by changing the state of the Pokémon card. When a phase is successfully defeated, the battle ends and Necrozma proceeds to its next phase permanently.
Phase 1 → Phase 2 (Use the Sun/Moon coin to determine which form to battle) → Phase 3
In this game, the game changes the phase and tosses the Sun/Moon coin for you.
You can now travel to the Distortion World using the 4 Distortion Gates found across the map.
Each Distortion Gate links to its exact counterpart and does not cost a tile move to use (for example, you can freely travel between the two Deepmarsh Gates).
One of the two Deepmarsh Gates.
The Ultra Megalopolis allows you to fully restore your party and trade with the Ginkgo Merchants once per turn like villages do, however you cannot fly to or from there.
The Ultra Megalopolis can be selected as a home village and has its own trainer token that starts there.
Ultra Megalopolis
These act like normal Apricorn Trees but offer a mixed selection of both Pokémon and Apricorns.
The rewards are based on the encounter tier of the Pokémon you choose to battle.
Warped Apricorn Tree
The Lake Guardians (Mesprit, Uxie, Azelf) can now be battled independently at each Lake Cavern.
However, they are immune to capture attempts and all damage until the turn after their trials are overcome:
Lake Verity Cavern

items.text: Trial of Emotion: Mesprit must take damage from battle fatigue.
Trial of Knowledge: Uxie must be attacked with 2 different types that are super effective.
Trial of Willpower: Azelf must be attacked with 2 or more critical hits over your last 2 turns.

blocks.text: After each Lake Guardian is defeated or captured, all trainers gain +2 movement per turn for the rest of the game.
Arceus is understandably wary of getting involved again after the events that occurred a decade ago.
He has however sent another Pokémon in his stead to the Temple of Sinnoh. Defeating or capturing this Pokémon grants 1 Blessing of Arceus.
The Temple of Sinnoh

blocks.q: Do I get all 3 Apricorns from an Apricorn Tree/Reef if no wild Pokémon appear during the Pokédex search?
blocks.text: You may, however your turn ends after doing so.

blocks.q: What happens when I teach a Pokémon a compatible move before it evolves, but after it evolves the move is no longer compatible?
blocks.text: Keep the move but you cannot learn any more moves of the incompatible type.

blocks.q: How many Poké Balls can I carry?
blocks.text: As many as you like (you can use the Poké Ball slot on your bag to store them), although you cannot convert them back into Apricorns.

blocks.q: How many Held Items can I carry?
blocks.text: As many as you like (you can use the Held Item slot on your bag to store them), although you cannot use the effect of any Held Items that are not attached to a Pokémon.

blocks.q: What happens if it is not feasible for either Pokémon to do damage to the other?
blocks.text: After 5 rolls in a row, battle fatigue starts taking effect dealing 3 damage each time the dice are rolled. This should end the battle. In case it does not, you may invoke a final clause that causes both Pokémon in the battle to faint from exhaustion.

blocks.q: Can continue interacting with Hidden Spots on my turn?
blocks.text: Yes, battling is the only thing that ends your turn early.

blocks.q: Can I release my Pokémon?
blocks.text: Yes, if it is not your last Pokémon, any Pokémon can be released.

blocks.q: Can I transfer my moves around my team?
blocks.text: No, however you can replace or discard already learnt moves.

blocks.q: Can I send out another Pokémon if a wild Pokémon defeats one of mine?
blocks.text: Not unless the wild Pokémon is a Legendary Pokémon or you have used an effect that prevents the wild Pokémon from fleeing.

blocks.q: How do I change my player colour ?
blocks.text: Once you have selected a home village card, put this card in your hand area and it will automatically change your hand colour to match the card. You will need to reselect your seat after doing so (make sure that another player has not already selected your colour as well).

blocks.q: Why does my Poké Ball keep changing its occupant when I hover over other Pokémon?
blocks.text: You likely need to increase your lift height in TTS, otherwise the Poké Ball will clip the other Pokémon zones when being moved around.
In this game, the game handles player colours and moving Poké Balls for you.

If you were unable to find the answer to your question here, I encourage you to use your best judgement before asking in the #help channel of the Discord server. The channel is not a replacement for reading the rules.
I hope you enjoyed your playthrough of Pokémon: Legends of Sinnoh, I appreciate you taking the time to play it!

Each trainer is granted two special abilities that are unlocked over the course of the game

Before the game begins, deal 3 trainer cards to each trainer. When choosing a starter Pokémon, each trainer also chooses one of the trainer cards to place face up in their trainer area. Unused cards are returned to the deck.

Trainer cards start out as Bronze (State 1) with both abilities locked. Once you defeat or obtain 1 Moderate Pokémon, upgrade to the Silver card (State 2) unlocking the "Blue" ability. Similarly, once you defeat or obtain 1 Strong Pokémon, upgrade to the Gold card (State 3) unlocking the "Red" ability also.
In this game, the game deals the trainer cards and upgrades them for you.
EXPERIMENTAL
When fighting the Ultra Beasts or Necrozma, draw and play 1 Ultra Onslaught card at the start of each of their turns.
Discard any played cards. If the deck is out of cards, shuffle the discard pile back into the deck.
In this game, when Ultra Onslaught is turned on, the game draws and discards the cards for you.
